description_full: TIM S.A. engages in the telecommunications sector in Brazil. It offers landline switched telephone services in local, national, and international long-distance modes, as well as personal mobile and multimedia communication services. The company is based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. TIM S.A. is a subsidiary of TIM Brasil Serviços e Participações S.A.
ceo_bio: Mr. Alberto Mario Griselli | President, CEO & Director | Age 56
financial_summary: TIM S.A. is a mid-cap communication services business with a $8.7B market cap on $4.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 16% against a 8% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 53% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.5B in free cash flow — roughly 33 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.12× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 1.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 6.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 24% operating margin runs 15pp above the Communication Services median (8%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.16x).
It accounts for 0.2% of sector revenue and 0.2% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 172 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 13% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 6% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 35% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 37% and a beta of 0.55, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.12 vs 5y 0.40), so read it loosely.
About $10.5M trades a day, enough to build a position, and interest is running hot at 1.8x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 48% in the 2020 crash, 28% in the 2022 bear market and 73% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 75% below its DCF fair value of $71.66, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 31%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $53.24 to $102 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Communication Services peers: P/E 11.1 vs 14.1, EV/EBITDA 1.7 vs 9.9 and P/FCF 5.8 vs 10.6 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 8% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 17.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.5% (vs the 8% bar).
The 7 covering analysts target $22.98 on average, 26% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 16% clears the cost of capital of 8.1% by 8pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.31).
It runs a 53% gross margin and converts 33% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 3.12x.
ROE of 18% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.4x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $139.8M.
The current ratio of 0.89 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 4.5% over 3 years and 7.1% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 11.2% a year over five years.
It has missed earnings estimates by 2.2% on average.
Analysts expect 12.3% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.0%), and institutions hold 5%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (10 sales, net $756K sold).
It returns 6.0% a year to shareholders (7.6% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 27 consecutive years, raising it 21.2% a year over the last five.
